answer: An identity must present a ring-signature history: signatures made as part of real rings, over years, with the rings themselves public. A vault holds what is precious, and a ring history is precious because it cannot be faked: every signature is on the record. The karst of a farm's rings is hollow: their rings are all formed last month, all with the same members, all with no real transactions. A relic is trusted because it has survived, and a ring history spanning years is the same: the network trusts the signer whose rings show a life, not a farm's empty circles.
